source.title: From Theory to Decision Rule: Calibrating the Noisy-Label Crossover for Vision-Language Model Weak Supervision Across Three Medical-Imaging Benchmarks
source.authors: Bruce Changlong Xu; Jose K. James; Alexander J. Ryu

page_placements.theme: Corruption structure matters beyond its rate

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares students trained with synthetic rate-matched random label corruption against students trained with structured VLM labels, and reports test AUC. It does not measure fitting completely random labels or the claim versions’ other named outcomes.
record.gate_note: Table 4 reports outcomes for rate-matched random label corruption, but not training error, convergence time, or test error under completely random labeling. Other results about mixed gold/weak supervision do not directly measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study measures test AUC under structured VLM supervision versus partially corrupted labels at fixed noise rates. It reports no training-label fit, corruption-fraction sweep, convergence comparison, or learning-order measurements. Neither its experiments nor its theoretical crossover argument tests V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that VLM weak labels help at scarce gold-label budgets but impose a teacher-dependent generalization ceiling; they propose a validation-AUC decision rule for choosing whether to add weak labels. They do not conclude that students fit completely random labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains students on mixtures of expert gold labels and weak labels from a VLM or rate-matched synthetic corruption, and reports test AUC; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, gold-label budget, weak-label source and rate, student architecture, VLM prompt, and training objective affect reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched nominal noise rates, structured VLM labels yield lower test AUC than random flips on PCAM and ISIC, but higher macro-AUC on NIH-CXR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization effect of structured versus random label corruption depends on the dataset and target-label structure: structured-minus-random AUC ranges from −0.111 to −0.090 on PCAM, −0.195 to −0.075 on ISIC, and +0.027 to +0.044 on NIH-CXR.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted at the ICML 2026 Workshop on Combining Theory and Benchmarks (CTB), as stated in the text.
record.problems: Table 4 does not state the student backbone in its caption or rows; several PCAM entries report no uncertainty; the study does not measure training error or convergence on completely random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No additional Table 4 rows left out. Other tables report gold/weak mixtures and decision-rule or loss comparisons, not outcomes measuring a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random training labels to zero or near-zero error, chance test performance, and preservation of architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence slowdown with increasing corruption.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steady test-error degradation across a corruption-fraction sweep from none to all. Varying gold and weak sample counts at fixed corruption rates does not establish this.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether its removal impairs true-label generalization.
The temporal order of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. The reported AUC ceilings concern generalization under weak supervision and do not establish limits on memorizing training labels.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test completely random labels, training error, test error at chance, or whether architecture and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.
Training time and convergence speed are not reported.
Does not report shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Does not sweep the fraction of corrupted labels from none to all or report training error across such a sweep.
Does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting, or whether removing them affects true-label generalization.
Does not measure the order in which real and noisy labels are learned over training.

tranche.reason: The study measures test AUC under structured weak labels and rate-matched partial corruption. Neither its experiments nor its theory tests or uses any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: Table 4 does not identify its PCAM student backbone or display PCAM standard deviations. Its ng=50 delta is reported as −0.100, although the displayed AUC values subtract to −0.099; the checked values and statement's range remain correct.
